steps.premise: A cloth that fits the top can hang uncomfortably low.
steps.action: List how far each cloth hangs over the hall's usual tables.
steps.consequence: Borrowers can choose one that leaves guests room at the knees.
steps.quote: A cloth can cover the tabletop and still hang too low over a guest's knees. List the drop for each cloth on the hall's usual tables so borrowers can choose a comfortable fit.

steps.premise: Returned linen has to be washed before the following booking.
steps.action: Allow time for drying and folding in the booking calendar.
steps.consequence: The next group is offered linen that can actually be ready.
steps.quote: A Saturday return still has to go through the wash. Block out drying and folding time on the booking calendar so Sunday's group is offered only what can be ready.

steps.premise: The hall and borrower need a quantity to check after dinner.
steps.action: Count napkins together at pickup and record the total on the slip.
steps.consequence: Both know how many napkins to find.
steps.quote: Count napkins together at pickup and write the number on the loan slip. Both sides then know what quantity to look for at the end of dinner.

steps.premise: Storeroom light makes similar dark colors hard to distinguish.
steps.action: Let borrowers examine a fabric swatch in daylight.
steps.consequence: They can select their intended color.
steps.quote: Navy and charcoal can look identical in the storeroom. A swatch borrowers can take into daylight helps them pick the color they intended.

steps.premise: A volunteer may come on foot for a bulky order.
steps.action: Include the packed crate count in the collection message.
steps.consequence: They can arrange transport if necessary.
steps.quote: A volunteer collecting a large wedding order may arrive on foot. Include the number of packed crates in the pickup note so they can arrange a ride if needed.

steps.premise: Hall linens and a caterer's linens can get mixed in the laundry.
steps.action: Put a washable ownership mark in a corner of the hall's cloths.
steps.consequence: The caterer can sort the pieces by owner.
steps.quote: A washable hall mark in one corner helps a caterer sort the hall's cloths from their own when both sets turn up in the same laundry load.

steps.premise: Bits of food and utensils can remain inside folded cloths.
steps.action: Have the clearing crew shake each cloth over a bin before putting it in the bag.
steps.consequence: Only fabric reaches the washing machine.
steps.quote: Crumbs and a forgotten dessert fork can disappear inside a folded cloth. Ask the clearing crew to shake each one over a bin before bagging it so the washer gets fabric alone.

steps.premise: Damp cloths can develop a smell in a sealed sack.
steps.action: Provide hanging space for wet cloths during cleanup.
steps.consequence: They can air out before going back to the hall.
steps.quote: Wet cloths can sour in a closed sack. Give borrowers a place to hang them during cleanup so they can air out before the return trip.

steps.premise: Candle wax has spilled on a cloth.
steps.action: Flag that cloth with a note on its return tag.
steps.consequence: Laundry workers can attend to it before hot drying.
steps.quote: If a guest spills candle wax, a note pinned to the return tag tells the laundry team which cloth needs attention before it reaches a hot dryer.

steps.premise: A hem might tear while guests are at the table.
steps.action: Give the event lead a phone number for reporting the tear.
steps.consequence: Hall staff can arrange a replacement during use.
steps.quote: Give the event lead a number to call when a hem tears. Staff can arrange a replacement while guests are still using the affected table.

steps.premise: An embroidered cloth could snag on a rough packing crate.
steps.action: Cover the crate interior with a smooth lining.
steps.consequence: Threads stay intact while the cloth travels between buildings.
steps.quote: Rough crate edges can catch embroidery. Line the crates with smooth covers so moving a loan between buildings doesn't pull threads loose.

steps.premise: A new volunteer needs to put clean linen in its pickup location.
steps.action: Mark return bins with aisle and shelf numbers.
steps.consequence: The volunteer can shelve the pieces where the next order will be collected.
steps.quote: Put an aisle and shelf number on each return bin. A new volunteer can then put clean linen away where the next order will be picked.

steps.premise: Attendance may change after the invitations are sent.
steps.action: Set a deadline for confirming the final linen count.
steps.consequence: Staff still have time to change the order.
steps.quote: A booking for forty guests can grow after invitations go out. Set a date for the borrower to confirm the final quantity while staff still have time to adjust the order.

steps.premise: Used napkins can look like unused extras once bagged.
steps.action: Provide a distinct bag for unused spares.
steps.consequence: Staff can tell which napkins were untouched when they come back.
steps.quote: A bag of used napkins looks much like one that never left the cupboard. Supply a separate bag for untouched spares so they can be identified on return.

steps.premise: A fold can conceal a stain.
steps.action: Spread each tablecloth out in bright light before packing.
steps.consequence: The borrower can receive a presentable set.
steps.quote: A stack can look spotless while a mark hides inside a fold. Open each tablecloth under a bright light before packing it so the borrower gets a presentable set.

steps.premise: The main hall may be locked when a newcomer comes to collect linens.
steps.action: Include a photo of the collection entrance in the pickup email.
steps.consequence: New borrowers can go directly to the linen room.
steps.quote: Put a picture of the collection door in the pickup email. First-time borrowers can go straight to the linen room even when the main hall is locked.

steps.premise: An event uses tables of several shapes.
steps.action: Group linens for packing by room and table number.
steps.consequence: The setup crew can deliver each bundle straight to its table.
steps.quote: When a group's tables have different shapes, pack by room and table number. Its setup crew can take each bundle straight to the right spot.

steps.premise: An accident could spoil a cloth just before the event.
steps.action: Hold a few plain replacement cloths in reserve.
steps.consequence: The group can re-cover the affected table before guests arrive.
steps.quote: Reserve a small supply of plain cloths for last-minute mishaps. A group that overturns a jug during setup can cover the table again before guests arrive.

steps.premise: Clean cloths at the bottom of a stack may go unused for months.
steps.action: Put newly washed cloths behind stock that was cleaned earlier.
steps.consequence: The stock wears more evenly.
steps.quote: Cloths at the bottom of a pile may sit unused for months. Put freshly laundered pieces behind the older clean ones so wear is shared across the stock.

steps.premise: The hall has checked the loan back in.
steps.action: Send the group a receipt for the return.
steps.consequence: The group can close its records knowing whether it still needs to find anything.
steps.quote: Send a return receipt after the hall checks in the loan. The group can close its event file knowing whether it still needs to search for a missing piece.
